parole.significato: ram (a male sheep), wether (a castrated ram)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Romanian berbec (“ram”), ultimately from Vulgar Latin vervex (“wether, ram”). First attested in 1423.
First attested in 1509. Borrowed from Romanian sâmbră, from Proto-Slavic *sębrъ.
From Romanian drujbă (“chainsaw”).

parole.testo: Borrowed from Romanian stână (“a summertime settlement of shepherds, sheepfold”). First attested in 1583.

parole.significato: hora (Romanian folk dance or its music)
parole.testo: From Romanian horă, from Greek χορός (chorós, “dance”).
Borrowed from Romanian cabană (“hut, cabin, chalet”).
From Romanian clacă (“joint voluntary work”), from a Slavic language, compare Bulgarian тлака (tlaka, “joint voluntary work, evening gathering”).

From Romanian cașcaval (“kashkaval”), from Ottoman Turkish قاشقوال (kaşkaval), from Italian caciocavallo (“a type of South Italian cheese”) (literally, "horse cheese"), from cacio (“cheese”) + cavallo (“horse”). Modern Turkish spelling is kaşkaval.

parole.testo: First attested in 1648. Borrowed from Romanian cumpănă, from Old Church Slavonic кѫпона (kǫpona) from Latin campāna.

parole.significato: goose egg (a swelling caused by a bump on the head)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Romanian cucui (“bump on the head”).

From Romanian leuștean, probably a borrowing of Hungarian lesten, variant of obsolete levestikom, from Late Latin levisticum (“lovage”), probably an alteration of Latin ligusticum (“Ligurian”).

parole.significato: sturdy (of small build but thick-set and hardy)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Romanian mocan (“Transylvanian mountain shepherd”), from moacă (“club, cudgel”). The adjective senses originated mainly in Hungarian. First attested in 1678.

From Romanian păcură (“oil, tar”), from Late Latin picula, diminutive of Latin pix (“pitch, tar”).
Borrowed from Romanian plăcintă, from Latin placenta (“cake”).

parole.testo: Borrowed from Romanian performant (“efficient, performant”), from French performant (“efficient, performant”). With -áns ending.
From Romanian prunc (“infant, baby”), from Late Latin *puerunculus ("small child"), from Latin puer (“boy”).

parole.significato: bag (soft container made out of cloth, paper, thin plastic, etc.)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Romanian pungă (“bag, purse”).

parole.significato: Romanian (of, from, or relating to Romania, its people or language)
parole.testo: From Romanian român (“Romanian”), from Latin Rōmānus (“Roman”).
From Romanian tilincă, titilincă (“flute”), of onomatopoeic origin. Compare Spanish tilín (“ting-a-ling, tinkle”).

parole.significato: Strips of meat stewed on fried onion, black pepper and marjoram. A kind of "pörkölt" that does not contain paprika and…
parole.testo: From Romanian tocană (“meat stew, goulash”), from toca (“to chop, mince”), from Vulgar Latin *toccare (“to knock, strike”).
Borrowed from Romanian vânătă (“eggplant”).

parole.significato: Vaccinium, a genus of shrubs in the plant family Ericaceae including the bilberry, bog bilberry, cowberry and cranberry.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Romanian. Compare Romanian afin (“cowberry”) and afină (“blueberry”). First attested in 1708.

parole.significato: Mason jar (glass jar with a screw top, often used for preserving food)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Romanian borcan (“jar”), of uncertain origin: an augmentative of boroacă (“swelling”); from Hungarian bokál (“pitcher”); or from Hungarian borkancsó (“wine pitcher”) or borkanna (“wine jug”).
